name: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings Ltd
title: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings Ltd - 504973 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Chola MS general insurance: combined ratio rose to 115.2% (112.2% ex-1/n) on motor OD and TP reserving, with ROE guidance softened to a medium-to-long-term 15%+ and no numeric combined-ratio guide.

triggers.label: Combined ratio 115.2% for FY26
triggers.quote: the combined ratio for the year was at 115.2% and 112.2% without the 1/n effect

triggers.label: Motor OD price realisation up 7-8%
triggers.quote: we have seen about 7% to 8% improvement in the price realization for us

triggers.label: ROE target softened to medium-to-long term

red_flags.quote: for us the delta has been about 10%

red_flags.label: Solvency down to 1.96x from 2.18x
red_flags.quote: We're bringing the solvency level down from 2.18x to 1.96x

summary.headline: Chola MS FY26 combined ratio rose to 115.2% (112.2% ex-1/n) on motor claims and crop loss; PBT Rs454 crore, ROE 10.4%.
summary.overview: Chola MS reported Q4 GDPI of Rs2,048 crore and FY26 GDPI of Rs7,762 crore, with the loss of crop business after re-tender cutting Rs124 crore in Q4 and over Rs590 crore for the year. The FY26 claims ratio rose about 2.71 percentage points, driven by motor OD claims and a stepped-up motor third-party reserve, pushing the combined ratio to 115.2%. FY26 PBT was Rs454 crore after labour-code gratuity provisioning, and ROE was 10.4% against a 3-year average peak of about 14.4%. Management will seek forbearance to move statutory accounting to Ind AS from April 1, 2027, and Rajive Kumaraswami takes over as MD from June 1.

financial_highlights.change: higher YoY; overall claims ratio up about 2.71 pp

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 ROE on average net worth

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Market share 5.25%; mix of cars 49%+, CVs 40%+, 2-wheelers about 10.5%. Motor OD share grew to about 5.89% while TP share fell about 0.5 pp. 2-wheeler share cut from 19.6% to about 10.6%.

segments.name: Long-term non-motor
segments.commentary: Premium received in advance rose to about Rs570 crore at March 2026 from Rs250 crore at March 2025. Non-motor market share 3.3% for the year, with premium received in advance of Rs410 crore for the year.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Lost crop business after re-tender, a hit of about Rs598 crore for FY26 per the Q&A. Management expects to participate in the next tender cycle across states, awaiting Government of India guidelines.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV book about 40-42% of motor mix and stable. Management sees pricing pressure and is managing line sizes while using newly secured reinsurance capacity on favourable terms.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal forward guidance on combined ratio; medium- to long-term intent is to maintain ROE of 15%+.
Motor OD price realisation up about 7-8% over the last 2-3 months; management expects motor OD loss ratio to start falling within about 6 months.
Statutory accounting to move to Ind AS from April 1, 2027 (FY28) under forbearance; significant drop in combined ratio expected in the year of adoption, then levelling out.
Management expects the 30% EOM norm to remain without further glide path; any regulator-mandated cut in commissions seen as positive, though it may lower premiums and float income.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity secured during the year on favourable terms, supporting commercial growth.
Chola Xceed operating app for sales staff and channel partners to launch soon, aimed at renewals and productivity.
Agency channel base built up; focus shifts to renewal rates.
Dividend withheld, with earnings retained to support growth and solvency.
demand_pricing: Direct premium declined in FY26; GWP growth came mainly from reinsurance inward business.
Motor TP premium unchanged for about 4-5 years; management is pressing regulator and government for two-way TP pricing correction.
Motor OD claims ratio rose across industry; Chola's rise about 10% versus about 5-7% for peers, per management.
Retail retention about 78%+ on weighted basis; blended retention about 72%.
Management says expected IFRS adoption (DAC and discounting of motor TP) will benefit P&L.

qa_highlights.question: Will the approach change under EOM compliance, and which lines will recover market share for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects crop business to return from the next tender cycle and aims to grow direct crop; motor 2-wheeler cut is near its floor; car and CV books to keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROE rise to 16-17% if leverage falls to 5.5% and combined ratio is 108-109%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the OD claims ratio is the area of correction (about 10% above peers), with 7-8% price realisation gains and a target ROE of about 15%. TP reserving is prudent and cash is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: What will the claims ratio look like under Ind AS/IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Motor TP provisions are discounted under IFRS, which brings a significant one-time benefit on transition and later P&L benefit through the unwind; no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did solvency drop to 1.96x and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher claims growth consumed more capital; solvency should recover with better claims ratio and retained earnings.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No combined ratio guidance; will aim for 15%+ ROE medium to long term, managing float income and combined ratio as EOM changes.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio recovery depends on the 7-8% price correction holding over the next 6 months.
Motor TP pricing remains unrevised; rising court awards and minimum wage hikes could push severity higher.
Possible regulator-mandated commission cuts could reduce premiums and float income.
Crop tender outcome and timing uncertain; GWP growth depends on winning back crop business.
Ind AS transition in FY28 creates accounting uncertainty; forbearance sought.
Solvency at 1.96x, below the historical 2.0-2.15x range.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on FY26 claims and combined ratio, acknowledging the OD loss ratio as an area of correction. Confident on the long-term franchise, retention, and IFRS benefit, but avoids forward combined ratio guidance and gives only a medium- to long-term 15%+ ROE aim.
key_quotes: So I think there, we will continue to grow.
And that is an area of correction for us, which we have already commenced the necessary activities to bring down the loss ratio.
So whatever it takes, whether it is managing float income or combined ratio, we will work towards getting to that objective.

growth.why: No formal revenue or GWP guidance; direct premium declined in FY26 and GWP growth came mainly from reinsurance inward, with the crop loss (about Rs598 crore hit) and motor pricing pressure weighing, so the call points to flat-to-weak growth, while management only holds a 15%+ medium-to-long-term ROE goal and cites motor OD price realisation of 7-8% and reinsurance capacity as support.

mgmt.note: Rajive Kumaraswami takes over as MD from June 1, 2026; the brief gives no stated growth plan from him.
